questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

In production Kubernetes environments, ensuring supply-chain security for Helm-based deployments is critical. This question evaluates your ability to integrate multiple security tools—Helm templating, SBOM generation, and image signature verification—into a cohesive CI gate. It tests practical knowledge of enforcing provenance and attestations before code merges.

## Key Concepts

- **Helm templating and values extraction**: Rendering charts to discover all container images referenced in deployments
- **SBOM generation**: Using Syft to create a CycloneDX SBOM that catalogs all dependencies and artifacts
- **Image signing verification**: Using cosign to validate container image signatures against a public key stored in the repository
- **CI gate integration**: Implementing fail-fast behavior in GitHub Actions to block unsigned images and missing attestations

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for Helm image signing enforcement
name: Helm Image Security Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  helm-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Install Helm and Syft
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh

      - name: Render Helm templates
        run: helm template my-app ./chart --values values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered

      - name: Extract image references
        run: |
          grep -rh 'image:' ./rendered | awk '{print $2}' > images.txt

      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft $(cat images.txt) -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Verify image signatures with cosign
        run: |
          COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub
          for IMAGE in $(cat images.txt); do
            cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE || exit 1
          done
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical security controls: CI image signing, tag governance, and runtime enforcement with Kyverno; it requires understanding Cosign, Rekor, image verification, and policy-as-code interplay, plus how to craft minimal manifests and verify locally, in CI, and at runtime.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Tag policy regex
- Kyverno image verification at admission
- Minimal manifest testing (unsigned vs signed)
- CI and runtime integration and trade-offs (latency, private registries)

## Code Example

```yaml
# CI workflow snippet (Cosign verify)
name: CI Image Sign Check
on: pull_request
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v1
      - name: Verify signatures
        run: |
          cosign verify registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (illustrative)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: verify-signed-image
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validateImages:
      - image: "*"
        cosign:
          publicKey: |
            -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
            ...
            -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (unsigned image)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ride-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ride
        image: registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (signed image)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ride-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ride
        image: registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0-signed
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question rigorously tests practical CI security knowledge for multi-tenant infrastructure, covering both container images and WASM modules deployed across edge and cloud environments. It evaluates understanding of supply chain security, provenance verification, and admission control policies.

## Key Concepts
- **Cosign Verification**: Cryptographic signing and verification for OCI container images and WASM modules using key pairs
- **SBOM Enforcement**: Requiring Software Bill of Materials for dependency transparency and vulnerability tracking
- **Rekor Attestations**: Immutable transparency log verification for artifact provenance
- **Manifest Validation**: Ensuring Kubernetes manifests reference only cryptographically verified signed artifacts
- **Admission Control**: Kyverno or OPA policies for runtime enforcement in Kubernetes clusters
- **GitHub Actions**: CI/CD workflow implementation for automated security gates

## Implementation Overview
The solution requires:
1. Cosign key pair management with public key distributed across CI/CD and cluster admission controllers
2. SBOM generation during build (using tools like Syft or SPDX)
3. Rekor integration for attestation verification
4. Policy engine (Kyverno/OPA) to validate signed references at admission time
5. Local developer verification scripts using cosign CLI

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce cross-cloud data provenance and model lineage for ML workloads; ensures reproducibility and auditing of deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper
- Image digests, internal registries, provenance annotations
- MLflow tracking integration and run_id propagation
- Local and CI validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Fail
  rules:
  - name: require-provenance-annotations
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Missing provenance annotations: model_version, dataset_hash, training_run_id'
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            model_version: '*'
            dataset_hash: '*'
            training_run_id: '*'
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Container image must include a digest'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '*@*'
```

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-inference-fail

        app: ml

      containers:

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to enforce end-to-end data provenance and reproducibility across hybrid multi-tenant environments, combining image signing, SBOM management, and centralized provenance tracking to guard against tampered or non-reproducible artifacts.

## Key Concepts
- End-to-end data provenance across on-prem and cloud environments
- Reproducible builds with digests tied to provenance records
- Attestation formats (SBOM via CycloneDX) and cryptographic signing (Sigstore/cosign)
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control
- CI/CD pipeline integration (GitHub Actions) and runtime verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for ML model artifact pipeline
name: Model Artifact Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['models/**']

jobs:
  build-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build model image
        run: |
          docker build -t model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} ./models/
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} -o cyclonedx-json > model.sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Attach SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cosign attest --type cyclonedx --key cosign.key \
            --predicate model.sbom.json model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Upload provenance
        run: |
          curl -X POST $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL/attestations \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -d '{"digest":"'$GITHUB_SHA'","sbom":"model.sbom.json","signature":"cosign"}'
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy for admission control
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-model-admission
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-cosign-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "Model image must be cosign-signed"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
    - name: verify-sbom-attestation
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "SBOM attestation required"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
```

## Verification Steps

**Local Verification:**
```bash
# Verify cosign signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:latest

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:latest

# Check reproducibility digest
reproctl verify --provenance $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL
```

**CI Verification:**
```yaml
verify-attestations:
  needs: build-and-sign
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - name: Verify all attestations
      run: |
        cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
        cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
```

## Why This Question Is Asked
This tests practical policy design, edge-case handling, and CI integration for Kubernetes manifests in a multi-team environment. Candidates must demonstrate understanding of resource isolation, pod hardening, network security, and hardware scheduling constraints.

## Key Concepts
- **ResourceQuota and LimitRange**: Prevent resource starvation and enforce default resource requests/limits per namespace
- **Pod securityContext**: Enforce runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and capability dropping for workload hardening
- **Ingress TLS with cert-manager**: Ensure encrypted external traffic with automated certificate management
- **GPU scheduling constraints**: Use nodeSelector and resource requests to restrict GPU workloads to approved namespaces and nodes
- **CI validation**: Integrate Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper with kubectl dry-run for pre-merge enforcement

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy for ML Platform Gates
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-platform-gates
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
    - name: require-resource-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Namespace]
      validate:
        message: "Each namespace must have a ResourceQuota."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              quota-ready: "true"

    - name: require-security-context
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      validate:
        message: "Containers must run as non-root with read-only filesystem and drop ALL capabilities."
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: [ALL]

    - name: require-ingress-tls
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Ingress]
      validate:
        message: "Ingress must use TLS with cert-manager annotation."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              (cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer): "?*"
          spec:
            tls:
              - secretName: "?*"

    - name: gpu-in-approved-namespaces
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      preconditions:
        - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
          operator: In
          value: ["1", "2", "4"]
      validate:
        message: "GPU pods are only allowed in approved namespaces with nvidia nodeSelector."
        pattern:
          spec:
            nodeSelector:
              nvidia.com/gpu: "?*"
```

## Verification Strategy

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical expertise in multi-tenant security, using real-world tools (cosign, Rekor, Kyverno, KMS) to enforce image provenance at CI time. It emphasizes tenant isolation, key management, and concrete verification steps.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign-based image signing with per-tenant keys stored in a central KMS
- Rekor-backed provenance verification
- Kyverno policy enforcing signatures and digest pinning across repos
- CI gating via GitHub Actions, plus local verification workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions gate (high level)
name: Image Signatures Gate
on: pull_request
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install cosign
        run: curl -fsSL https://toolkit.cosign.is/cosign-linux-amd64 -o /usr/local/bin/cosign && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cosign
      - name: Fetch tenant key from KMS
        run: |
          echo "Fetching tenant key..." # placeholder
      - name: Verify images in manifests
        run: |
          cosign verify --key <tenant-key> image digest
```
```yaml
# Kyverno policy snippet (digest-signature & tag checks)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-cosign-signature
spec:
  rules:
  - name: image-signature
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment, Job, KnativeService]
    validate:
      message: "Image must be cosign-signed with tenant key"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: ?*
              - imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```
